create.name: WCCM D-A-CH (Christian Meditation in Germany, Austria and Switzerland)
create.bio:
WCCM D-A-CH brings together the German, Austrian and Swiss communities of the World Community for Christian Meditation. It teaches the contemplative prayer renewed by the Benedictine John Main, who learned to meditate in Malaysia and later found the same path in the writings of John Cassian: sitting in silence twice a day and inwardly repeating the prayer word maranatha. It describes itself as an open community without formal membership that adds a contemplative element to church life rather than forming a new church, and it values dialogue with meditators of other faiths.

A volunteer team coordinates groups and events across the three countries, supported by a German-Austrian society and a Swiss association. It holds meditation days in German and French, such as Advent days in central Switzerland and Geneva, and residential seminars in Germany. Its website offers a practical introduction to the practice and a collection of texts and materials for groups. The Swiss association is registered in Peseux, near Neuchâtel.

courses.title: Meditationstag zum 1. Advent 2026
courses.description: A day of silent meditation, talks and sharing on the first Sunday of Advent at the Missionshaus Bethlehem in Immensee, led by José Amrein-Murer.

courses.title: Journée de l'Avent 2026
courses.description: A French-language Advent day of meditation and reflection at the Cénacle in Geneva with Marie-Dominique Minassian; the fee is a guide and people give what they can.

courses.title: Meditationsseminar in Oberzell 2027
courses.description: A residential weekend seminar of meditation and teaching in Oberzell, Germany, led by Sr Mechthild Brömel.

free_resources.title: Christliche Meditation lernen – Praxis und Anleitung
free_resources.description: A German introduction to the practice with step-by-step guidance and a printable leaflet.

free_resources.title: Materialien
free_resources.description: Texts and materials in German and French for meditators and group leaders.
